title: Delilah (Judges 16:4–21)
hookLine: strength given away a secret at a time

lines: TELL ME WHERE YOUR STRENGTH LIES.
cards: In the valley of Sorek lives a woman named Delilah, and the lords of the Philistines come to her with an offer. Find out where Samson's great strength lies, and each of us will give you eleven hundred pieces of silver.
The text says Samson loved her. It never says she loved him. And she doesn't hide what she's doing.
She asks him straight out: tell me, I pray thee, wherein thy great strength lieth, and how you could be bound.

teach.b: He lies. Bind me with fresh bowstrings, and I'll be weak. She does, with men lying in wait in the room, and cries: the Philistines are upon you, Samson.
He snaps them like thread. Again: new ropes, never used. He snaps those too.
The third time, listen. Weave the locks of my hair into the loom.

teach.h: THE THIRD LIE IS ABOUT HIS HAIR.
teach.b: Still a lie, but drifting toward the truth: now it's about his hair.

teach.h: HOW CANST THOU SAY, I LOVE THEE?
teach.b: Then she presses him: "How canst thou say, I love thee, when thine heart is not with me?" She pressed him daily, the text says, until his soul was vexed unto death. And he tells her everything.

No razor has come on my head; I've been a Nazirite to God from my mother's womb. Some readers hear the strength living not in the hair itself, but in the vow his mother was given, with the hair as its sign.
She lulls him to sleep on her knees and calls a man to shave him. When she cries, the Philistines are upon you, he wakes and thinks, I'll go out as at other times and shake myself free.

teach.h: HE DID NOT KNOW THE LORD HAD GONE.
teach.b: Then the line that hurts: he did not know that the Lord had departed from him. Nobody took his strength in one blow. He handed it over a little at a time, each lie a step closer to the truth.

how: Jews read the Samson and Delilah chapters as part of the Former Prophets, and rabbinic commentary links Samson's strength to his Nazirite vow and asks why he gave his secret away.

o: a prophetess who warned Samson about the Philistines
the woman who pressed Samson until he told his secret
Samson's mother, visited twice by the angel

games.q: guard your strength — tap the pairs.
p: his hair woven into the loom
no razor: a Nazirite from the womb

s: the text says Delilah was a Philistine
it says she lived in the valley of Sorek; it never names her people.
Samson's third false answer was already about his hair
weave my locks into the loom: the lies drift toward the truth.
Samson knew at once that his strength was gone
he woke thinking he'd shake himself free, and did not know the Lord had departed from him.

games.q: you're Samson. three times you've lied, and three times the Philistines came. she asks again, every day: how can you say you love me? what do you do?
o: get up and leave the valley of Sorek.
games.why: worn down by her daily pressing, he tells her all his heart: no razor has ever come on his head. then she calls a man to shave him.

practice: Name one thing that holds you up, sleep, a friendship, a daily prayer, staying sober, a promise you keep, and look honestly for the small ways you've been giving it away, because someone asked or because saying no was tiring.
Don't scold yourself; just see it, and choose one small way to guard it.

wordCard.voice: Delilah. The woman of the valley of Sorek who asked again and again where Samson's strength lay, until he told her.

orig.note: Hebrew: Delilah, as her name is written in Judges 16; the text never explains it.

carryVoice: Your line: guard your strength. Even Samson didn't notice it slipping away. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: How canst thou say, I love thee, when thine heart is not with me?
